name: Flame ward belt
description: A grey web belt with a heavy black box at the buckle. A crossed-out flame on the lid glows violet, and the air around you feels cooler.
notes: Own model for the switched-on state: the crystal in the flame glows (`crystal-glow-violet`). A web belt 1.1 m long and 38 mm wide, laid flat in a U, outside up: the buckle run along +z and the tip run along -z, joined by the bend at +x, with a steel emitter box 90 by 64 mm on the buckle run at the right front, where the reference puts it beside the buckle. CHECK VOLUME (x5.3): the belt lies spread out, so its box is mostly air. A belt is the waist host: the box fills the right front, so four belt points take pouches: the left front on the buckle run's free end, the left hip on the tip run, the right hip past the box and the back at the bend. The reference covers the torso; a belt takes the waist slot. The reference's crystal is a made-up material; the model shows it as a crystal set in the lid's emblem. The field it projects is a powered effect with no content field yet, so the draft carries no `protects`. The reference lists it under tools; it is worn, so the draft files it as clothing. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Crystal wrist computer
description: A slim green slate on a black wrist strap, its face a pane of blue crystal. It still keeps time, stores notes and tracks your heartbeat, though there is nothing left for it to talk to.
notes: A 48 by 34 mm slate in a jade-green housing with a crystal face, lying face up on its plastic strap laid open 210 mm long. The reference covers the hands and marks it sided; it is worn on one wrist like a watch, so it takes `wrist`, as the diver's watch does, and sidedness has no content field. The name is ours; the reference's own name is a proper noun from its lore. `timekeeping` reuses the watches' quality; its notes, health and camera functions have no content field yet.
